comments.title: No License Agreement for Landscaping Within Electric Easements
comments.comment: Trees, vegetation, irrigation, and the detention pond — all proposed within the 5' electric easements — lack any executed or referenced license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires a license agreement obtained from and filed with Austin Energy Public Involvement before installing landscaping, trees, or irrigation within electric easement areas. The following deficiencies are present:
- Trees (types M — Mitigation, PL — Parking Lot, SY — Street Yard, P — Parking Buffer Point) and irrigation are proposed within the 5' electric easements along the southern, eastern, and northern property boundaries; trees along the southern boundary are positioned approximately 0.5 ft from the property line, placing them within the 5' easement
- The biofiltration/detention pond — which requires 95% vegetative cover per its maintenance specifications (Sheet 16) — is located within the 5' electric easement along the eastern boundary, constituting landscaping within the easement
- No executed license agreement is referenced on any plan sheet, in any plan note, or in any supplementary document; the landscape plan's irrigation notes section makes no mention of easement authorization
- The Consolidated Site Plan Application explicitly states 'No' to submitting a license agreement application
Missing license agreements result in certificate of occupancy holds; Austin Energy reserves the right to remove non-compliant landscaping at the owner's cost.
comments.sheets: Plat (Sheet 2); Site plan (Sheet 9); Biofiltration-Detention Pond Plan & Calculations (Sheet 15); Biofiltration-Detention Pond Profiles (Sheet 16); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Landscape plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: 5' electric easements (×2) along southern, eastern, and northern property boundaries, including biofiltration/detention pond area within eastern easement (Mecey Subdivision plat, Travis County Doc 73/76, Case C8S-75-160)
comments.resolution: Option A: Obtain an executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement authorizing the proposed landscaping, trees, and irrigation within the 5' electric easements; add a plan note on Sheets 9 and 31 stating 'License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement obtained prior to installation of any landscaping within electric easement areas' including the agreement date and number. Option B: Relocate all trees, vegetation, and irrigation systems entirely outside the 5' electric easement boundaries and revise Sheet 31 to overlay easement boundaries on the landscape plan confirming no encroachment.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Easement boundaries are not overlaid on the Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), making exact tree-to-easement overlap uncertain in some runs — verify precise encroachment against surveyed easement lines.

perRunFindings.comment: License agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement required if landscaping is within electric easement areas. Electric easement boundaries are not shown on Landscape Plan, and license agreement documentation is not evident in current submittal.
perRunFindings.observation: Plat (Sheet 2) shows 5-foot electric easements along northern and southern boundaries. Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) does not show electric easement boundaries. No license agreement documentation evident in current submittal.
perRunFindings.reasoning: If landscaping within electric easements, UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement. Plans do not show easement boundaries coordinated with Landscape Plan, and agreement documentation not evident in current submittal.

perRunFindings.comment: Obtain a License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement before installing any landscaping, trees, irrigation, or plantings within electric easement areas. Provide executed copy with final site plan submittal or reference execution in a plan note.
perRunFindings.observation: No executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement for landscaping, trees, or irrigation within electric easement areas. The Master Comment Report (Electric Review section) references UCM § 1.10.10.3. Sheet 31 shows trees proposed in areas where electric easements exist, but no evidence of the required license agreement.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 explicitly requires a License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement before installing landscaping within electric easement areas. The absence of this license agreement documentation is a deficiency.

perRunFindings.comment: Trees and vegetation are shown within the southern and eastern 5' electric easement areas without documentation of a license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement. Provide a copy of the executed license agreement authorizing landscaping and irrigation within these easements, or relocate all landscaping outside the easement boundaries.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 depicts multiple tree and vegetation symbols within the southern 5' electric easement along the southern property line and eastern 5' electric easement along the eastern property line. Sheet 31 confirms tree placement with symbols labeled 'M' (Mitigation Trees), 'PL' (Parking Lot Trees), and 'P' (Parking Buffer Point Trees). Landscape Plan contains 'IRRIGATION NOTES' but does not reference any license agreement from Austin Energy.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 is explicit: 'Landscaping and irrigation systems permissible within easements only with license agreement obtained from and filed with Austin Energy Public Involvement.' The site plan shows landscaping within easement boundaries but provides no documentation of an executed license agreement.

perRunFindings.comment: The detention pond with required vegetation is located within the 5' Electric Easement but no executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement is documented on the plans. Obtain and file license agreement with Austin Energy authorizing landscaping and vegetation within the easement, or relocate pond outside easement boundary.
applicableAreas: Biofiltration/detention pond area and eastern property boundary within 5' Electric Easement
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 16 maintenance requirements specify: 'No unvegetated area shall exceed ten (10) square feet' with 95% vegetative cover required per biweekly maintenance inspections in the first growing season. The pond is located within the 5' Electric Easement along the eastern boundary. Sheet 31 shows the pond area but contains no indication of a license agreement.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires a license agreement before installing any landscaping within electric easements. The detention pond's required vegetation (95% cover) constitutes landscaping within the electric easement. No evidence of an executed license agreement is provided.

perRunFindings.comment: Trees planted within the southern 5-foot electric easement on the landscape plan without evidence of a required Austin Energy Public Involvement license agreement. A license agreement must be obtained before installing landscaping or trees within electric easements per UCM § 1.10.10.3.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 depicts a 5-foot electric easement running along the southern property boundary, labeled '5' Elec. Easement' with plat references (Vol. 69, Pg. 14 and Vol. 73, Pg. 76). perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires a license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement before installing landscaping within electric easement areas. The proposed trees at approximately 0.5 ft from the southern property line are at or within the 5' easement. The absence of any executed license agreement, combined with the applicant's 'No' response in the site plan application, constitutes non-compliance.

perRunFindings.comment: License agreement not obtained from Austin Energy Public Involvement for landscaping and trees proposed within electric easements. Multiple trees are plotted within or adjacent to electric easement boundaries on the southern and northern property lines.

perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 explicitly requires a license agreement before installing landscaping within electric easement areas. Austin Energy reserves the right to remove any obstruction without fault, and property owners are responsible for all costs.

perRunFindings.comment: No License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement is evident for trees/landscaping proposed within electric easements. Sheet 31 shows trees (M for mitigation) around the site perimeter; Sheet 31 does not display easement boundaries overlaid with the landscape plan. perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires that before landscaping within electric easements the license agreement must be 'obtained and filed before the activity occurs.' perRunFindings.comment: Tree plantings and landscaping are shown within 5-foot electric easements on north, south, and east boundaries without documented evidence of executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement. Provide executed license agreement letter from Austin Energy Public Involvement confirming landscaping/irrigation within the easement has been 'obtained from and filed with' the City (not 'to be obtained'). Agreement must be attached to site plan submittal prior to approval.
applicableAreas: Tree plantings within 5-foot electric easements on northern, eastern, and southern property boundaries
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 31 shows tree plantings (M — mitigation, SY — street yard, PL — parking lot) positioned directly adjacent to and overlapping property boundary lines on the north, south, and east sides. Sheet 9 depicts 5-foot electric easements along these same property boundaries. No notes, callouts, or attached documentation on either sheet reference an executed license agreement. Sheet 9 note d states 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date' but does not address current compliance. Landscape plan 'IRRIGATION NOTES' reference TCEQ Chapter 344 compliance but make no reference to an easement license agreement.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 states that landscaping and irrigation are permissible within electric easements only with a license agreement obtained from and filed with Austin Energy Public Involvement. Without documented evidence of the executed license agreement, the landscaping plantings shown within the easements cannot be approved. This is a certificate of occupancy hold item.

comments.title: Improvements Within Electric Easements Block Required 24/7 Austin Energy Access
comments.comment: Concrete retaining walls, wood fence, the biofiltration/detention pond, and proposed trees within the 5' electric easements obstruct the 24/7 vehicular access required for Austin Energy personnel and equipment.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires that any landscaping or improvements within electric easements not restrict 24/7 vehicular access for Austin Energy personnel and equipment. The following features within the 5' electric easements obstruct this required access:
- Concrete retaining walls and a wood fence are drawn within the southern and eastern easements on Sheet 9, creating physical barriers along the easement corridor
- The biofiltration/detention pond, enclosed by a concrete retaining wall, is located within the eastern 5' electric easement and its maintenance specifications (Sheet 16) require 95% vegetative cover — dense vegetation and the retaining wall structure together prevent free vehicular traversal
- Proposed trees and landscaping are positioned throughout the easement boundaries (Sheet 31), further reducing available access width within the already narrow 5' easement corridors
No notation, callout, or specification on any sheet confirms that a continuous unobstructed drivable maintenance corridor is maintained within the easements.
comments.sheets: Site plan (Sheet 9); Biofiltration-Detention Pond Profiles (Sheet 16); Landscape plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: 5' electric easements along southern and eastern property boundaries; biofiltration/detention pond area within eastern 5' electric easement
comments.resolution: Relocate concrete retaining walls, wood fence, the detention pond, and all trees entirely outside the 5' electric easement boundaries to restore unobstructed 24/7 vehicular access; or provide a dimensioned plan with engineer's certification demonstrating that a minimum continuous clear drivable corridor is maintained along the full length of each easement for Austin Energy maintenance vehicles, including notation of the clear width provided. Note: runs identified minimum widths of 12 ft and 24 ft — confirm the applicable Austin Energy standard with the reviewing electric engineer.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Runs disagree on the minimum clear corridor width required (12 ft per run-1, 24 ft per run-3) — confirm applicable Austin Energy maintenance vehicle standard before issuing.

perRunFindings.comment: Retaining walls, fences, landscaping, and other improvements within the electric easements obstruct required 24/7 vehicular maintenance access for Austin Energy personnel and equipment. Ensure that easement areas remain completely clear of all obstructions and maintain a continuous, unobstructed access corridor at least 12 feet wide within the easement for Austin Energy maintenance activities.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 depicts concrete retaining walls, a wood fence, driveways, and sidewalks located within or directly overlapping the southern and eastern 5' electric easement boundaries. Retaining walls run parallel to easement boundaries at the perimeter, creating access restrictions. The wood fence is drawn directly within the eastern 5' easement area. No dimensions or callout indicate that a clear, continuous, drivable maintenance corridor is maintained. Landscaping (trees) also positioned within easement areas further reduces open access.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 states that landscaping within easements is permitted only 'if landscaping does not restrict 24/7 access.' Retaining walls and fences inherently restrict access. The site plan shows these features within the easement boundaries with no notation confirming a 24/7 maintenance access corridor.

perRunFindings.comment: The detention pond with required vegetation and concrete retaining walls within the 5' Electric Easement obstructs required 24/7 vehicular access for Austin Energy maintenance. Relocate pond outside the easement or demonstrate 24-foot minimum clear drivable surface for maintenance vehicle access across the easement width.
applicableAreas: 5' Electric Easement along eastern property boundary
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 confirms the detention pond retaining wall is within the 5' Electric Easement. Sheet 16 specifies pond requires vegetation maintenance with 95% cover and detailed biweekly and routine maintenance. Sheet 31 shows trees in the eastern boundary area near the pond. The concrete retaining wall physically encloses the pond area. While some access routes and a maintenance gate are shown, the required vegetation within the pond and the concrete retaining wall infrastructure obstruct free vehicular access for Austin Energy maintenance trucks to traverse the easement.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires that 'landscaping within easements must maintain 24/7 vehicular access for Austin Energy personnel and equipment.' A concrete retaining wall enclosing a pond combined with required dense vegetation (95% cover) creates a physical obstruction preventing free vehicular access across the easement.

perRunFindings.comment: Tree plantings shown within electric easements would obstruct 24/7 vehicular access required for Austin Energy maintenance. Relocate all trees and landscaping outside the 5-foot electric easement boundaries to maintain unobstructed access corridor, or provide engineer certification that design maintains minimum 12-foot clear width for maintenance vehicle access along entire easement length.
applicableAreas: Tree plantings and landscaping within 5-foot electric easements on property perimeters
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 31 depicts tree plantings positioned within the 5-foot electric easements running along the north, south, and east property boundaries. Trees are shown with canopy symbols (circles) that extend several feet from the trunk location. Sheet 9 shows that these easements run the full length of these property lines. Easement widths (5 feet) are minimal; tree canopies, trunks, and root systems would occupy much of this width, leaving insufficient space for a maintenance vehicle to traverse the easement.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires that landscaping within electric easements be positioned such that it does not restrict 24/7 vehicular access for Austin Energy personnel and equipment. Tree plantings within the 5-foot easement corridors, with typical canopy spreads of 20–40+ feet, would substantially obstruct this required access.

comments.title: Landscape Plan Does Not Show Transformer Locations for Access Verification
comments.comment: Transformer pad locations and required service vehicle access routes are not overlaid on the Landscape Plan, making it impossible to verify that proposed trees do not obstruct Austin Energy equipment access.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires that landscaping not restrict Austin Energy personnel and equipment access to transformers and electric facilities. Transformer pad locations shown on Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and site access routes shown on Sheet 9 are not overlaid or cross-referenced on Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan). Without this coordination, it cannot be confirmed that proposed trees do not encroach on service vehicle routes or required turning radii for Austin Energy bucket trucks (typically 40–50 ft turning radius).
comments.sheets: Site plan (Sheet 9); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Landscape plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: Transformer pad locations and service vehicle access routes throughout site; landscape areas adjacent to transformer pads shown on Sheet 21
comments.resolution: Add transformer pad locations and service vehicle access routes from Sheet 21 to Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) and verify that no proposed trees or plantings encroach on access lanes or turning radii required for Austin Energy service vehicles; add a note on Sheet 31 confirming that landscaping design maintains unobstructed Austin Energy equipment access to all transformer and electrical facility locations.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Run-1 was unclear due to inability to verify compliance without transformer locations on the landscape plan — confirm coordination between Sheets 21 and 31 before closing.

perRunFindings.comment: Unable to verify whether proposed trees block truck access to transformers or equipment set-up areas due to lack of electrical infrastructure and access route coordination on Landscape Plan.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows transformer locations throughout site. Sheet 31 shows proposed trees but does not coordinate with transformer locations or equipment access requirements. Cannot assess whether proposed plantings obstruct access without electrical infrastructure shown on Landscape Plan.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Cannot verify access compliance without showing transformer locations and required turning radii/access clearances coordinated with proposed tree locations on Landscape Plan.

perRunFindings.comment: Show transformer locations and required truck access routes on the landscape plan. Verify no trees block access lanes or turning radii required for Austin Energy service vehicles (typical 40–50 ft turning radius for bucket trucks).
applicableAreas: Transformer locations and access routes throughout site
perRunFindings.observation: Transformer pad locations from Sheet 21 and access routes from Sheet 9 are not overlaid on the landscape plan (Sheet 31). Without this coordination, it cannot be verified that proposed trees do not obstruct access routes or turning radii for bucket trucks used to service transformers and Austin Energy equipment.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 states that landscaping must not restrict Austin Energy personnel and equipment access. The landscape plan must show transformer locations and access requirements to demonstrate compliance. The absence of this coordination indicates non-compliance with the access requirement.
